content.text: {"primary_meaning":"Divine or eternal life given by God in and through Jesus Christ—salvation understood as restored communion with God, spiritually present now and fulfilled in resurrection.","primary_basis":["John 1:4 — “In him was life,” associating life with the incarnate Word.","John 5:21, 24-26 — the Son gives life and possesses life in himself; believers pass from death to life.","John 10:10, 28 — Jesus gives abundant and eternal life.","John 11:25-26 — Jesus declares, “I am the resurrection and the life.”","John 14:6 — Jesus declares, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”","John 17:3 — eternal life is defined relationally as knowing the Father and Jesus Christ.","Romans 6:4, 23 — believers walk in newness of life, and God’s gift is eternal life in Christ.","Colossians 3:3-4 — Christ is identified as the believer’s life.","1 John 1:1-2; 5:11-12, 20 — eternal life is manifested in Christ and possessed through the Son."] ,"alternatives":[{"meaning":"Christ himself as “the Life,” emphasizing his identity as the source, embodiment, and mediator of divine life rather than merely a gift he bestows.","basis":["John 11:25","John 14:6","Colossians 3:4","1 John 1:1-2"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Ordinary created or biological life—the animating breath and earthly existence bestowed and sustained by God. In many passages “life” is literal rather than symbolic.","basis":["Genesis 2:7","Job 33:4","Psalm 104:29-30","Acts 17:25, 28"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Resurrection life: bodily life restored after death, especially through participation in Christ’s resurrection.","basis":["John 5:28-29","John 11:25-26","Romans 6:4-9","1 Corinthians 15:20-23, 42-49"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Present spiritual renewal or sanctified conduct—“newness of life,” often contrasted with sin, alienation, or spiritual death.","basis":["Romans 6:4, 11-13","Romans 8:6, 10-11","Ephesians 2:1-5","Galatians 2:20"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"Covenant flourishing, wisdom, and righteousness: life as well-being, blessing, and the fruitful path produced by fidelity to God.","basis":["Deuteronomy 30:15-20","Proverbs 3:16-18","Proverbs 8:35","Proverbs 12:28","Psalm 16:11"],"prominence":"common"},{"meaning":"The Holy Spirit’s life-giving presence or power, particularly as the principle of spiritual and resurrection life.","basis":["John 6:63","Romans 8:2, 6, 10-11","2 Corinthians 3:6"],"prominence":"minority"},{"meaning":"Immortality or unending conscious existence considered chiefly as duration rather than communion with God or participation in Christ.","basis":["Matthew 25:46","John 3:16","Revelation 21:4"],"prominence":"common"}],"has_settled_consensus":false,"confidence":"high","notes":"There is a strong central Christian association between “life,” especially “the life” in Johannine or Christological language, and eternal/divine life in Christ. Nevertheless, the term is highly context-dependent and often denotes ordinary existence, present spiritual renewal, righteous flourishing, or bodily resurrection. Thus there is no single settled symbolic interpretation applicable to every biblical occurrence."}
